standard_prerequisites.name: The perfect objects form a strictly full, saturated triangulated subcategory of the derived category
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the subcategory in question contains the smallest such subcategory generated by the ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: The subcategory generated by an object is the union of its finite stages, the first stage containing every finite projective module placed in any degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the induction target and the base case of the induction.

standard_prerequisites.name: A complex concentrated in degrees from a to b sits in a distinguished triangle with its top term shifted and its truncation below the top degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Realizes the induction step, showing that the complex belongs to the next stage of the generated subcategory.

core_obligations: Record the structural facts that perfect objects form a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory and that the ring belongs to it, so that the inclusion of the generated subcategory holds (proof lines 20295-20302).

Reduce the reverse inclusion to the following claim: a perfect object represented by a complex concentrated in degrees from a to b with finite projective terms belongs to the stage of the generated subcategory indexed by the length of that interval (proof lines 20303-20312).
Prove the claim by induction on the length of the interval, using that the first stage contains every finite projective module placed in any degree for the base case (proof lines 20312-20315).

Perform the induction step with the distinguished triangle exhibiting the top term shifted and the truncation below it, apply the induction hypothesis to the truncation and the base case to the top term, and conclude that the complex lies in the next stage (proof lines 20315-20322).
proof_roadmap: Check the two structural properties of the perfect objects and the containment of the ring (proof lines 20295-20302).
Reduce to an induction on the length of the interval in which a representing complex lives (proof lines 20303-20312).
Close the induction with the truncation triangle and the base case of finite projective modules (proof lines 20312-20322).
difficulty_reason: The statement identifies the category of perfect objects over a ring with the smallest strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory generated by the ring itself, phrased as saying that the ring is a classical generator (statement lines 20287-20293). The proof records the two structural properties of the perfect objects, then reduces to the claim that a complex of finite projective modules concentrated in an interval of length n belongs to the n-th stage of the generated subcategory, which is proved by induction using the distinguished triangle of the top term and the truncation below it (proof lines 20295-20322). The three citations are to the definitions of saturated subcategories and of generation, and to the earlier statements establishing the structural properties, all carried as navigation stubs.
